messages.body_plain:
When you test outside irace you are using a different command than when you test within irace. I would paste the commands to be more precise, but since you took screenshots, I cannot copy the text. Look at the command quoted by irace and look at the command that you run after ">". They are not identical. Most likely you modified your program to accept the arguments that you used for testing, but irace is calling your program differently, so your program crashes or breaks somehow. The problem is in your program, not in irace.

I have built a small example for you. You need a C++11 compiler. It works with this parameter.txt:

# Notice the space after --param1 !
param "--param1 " r (-10,10)

You can test outside irace by running:

./target-runner.exe testConfig1 instance1 1234567 f1   --param1 2.9248

It is very basic, but I hope it helps you to understand how it should work.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: local minimum
messages.subject_clean: local minimum
messages.body_plain:
Hi Naama,

irace is designed to converge quickly so it is not surprising that it gets stuck on local optima. The restart mechanism should ideally help early stagnation. Look in the output of irace if restarts are being triggered. If not, then analyze why not (typical reason is that numerical values are different enough to not trigger it, you could play with digits to reduce the resolution of numerical parameters).

You will have to analyze a bit the output of irace to understand why irace is not finding the best possible solutions. But there are quite a few things to try:

* If the variance across instances/runs is high, then irace may miss the best configuration if the best was unlucky on a few runs. You could try increasing firstTest.
* If you are providing the manual configuration as a starting solution, and the final configuration is similar to the manual one, this may be biasing the search too strongly. You may wish to remove this and then perform more independent runs of irace with smaller budgets using different seeds for each run of irace.

* If you are providing the manual configuration as a starting solution, but it gets eliminated, then irace does not think it is good. You need to investigate why this happens.

* On the other hand, if you are not providing the manual configuration to irace, maybe you should to direct irace towards a good area of the search space.

* Make sure that the way you decide that the manual configuration is better is also the way that irace compares configurations. Otherwise, irace is not optimizing the same thing as you do.

* "better" must be statistically better. That is, the manual conf may have smaller mean, but the t-test used by irace may say that the difference is not significant, thus it is not actually better.

* If you define "better" on the test set, be sure that the manual configuration was not tuned for the test set. irace uses a different training set, so it doesn't overfit. It may be a good idea to compare manual and irace on a different sample of instances from the same problem, just to be sure that manual is indeed better.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: irace 3.1 (first version 3)
messages.subject_clean: irace 3.1 (first version 3)
messages.body_plain:
Dear irace users,

Version 3.1 of irace is available from CRAN:

https://cran.r-project.org/package=irace

This is a major release (we found a minor bug in 3.0 so, after fixing it, we raised the version number to 3.1) with many bugfixes and new features, but only minor (or no interface changes), thus we recommend all users to upgrade.

In addition to the changes below, there are many updates to the User Guide:

 <http://goog_749926522>
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/irace/vignettes/irace-package.pdf

Best wishes,

    Manuel López-Ibáñez and Leslie Pérez Cáceres.

3.1  (12/07/2018)

 * Use testthat for unit testing.                        (Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * Allow instances to be a list of arbitrary R objects (mlr bugfix).
                                                         (Manuel López-Ibáñez)

3.0  (05/07/2018)

 * irace now supports adaptive capping for computation time minimization.
   The default value of the testType option is t-test when adaptive capping
   is enabled. Please see the user-guide for details.
                                    (Leslie Pérez Cáceres, Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * The package contains an ablation() function implementing the ablation
   method for parameter importance analysis by Fawcett and Hoos (2016).
                                     (Leslie Pérez Cáceres, Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * New option 'postselection' executes a post-selection race.
                                                        (Leslie Pérez Cáceres)

 * At the end of each race, if the race stops before evaluating all instances
   seen in previous races, then the best overall may be different than the best
   of the race. We now print the best overall (best-so-far). Elites evaluated
   on more instances are considered better than those evaluated on fewer.
                                    (Manuel López-Ibáñez, Leslie Pérez Cáceres)

 * Last active parameter values of numerical parameters (i and r) are carried
   by the sampling model. When a value must be assigned and the parameter was
   previously not active, the sampling is performed around the last value.
                                   (Leslie Pérez Cáceres, Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * R help pages are now generated with Roxygen2.
                                   (Leslie Pérez Cáceres, Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * The user guide documents --version, --help, and --check.
                                                        (Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * A return value of "Inf" from targetRunner/targetEvaluation results in the
   immediate rejection of the configuration without any further evaluation.
   This is useful for handling unreliable or broken configurations that should
   not stop irace.                                     (Manuel López-Ibáñez)

 * Numerical parameters may be sampled on a logarithmic scale using "i,log"
   or "r,log".                                               (Alberto Franzin)

 * New target-runner.bat for Windows contributed by André de Souza Andrade.

 * Fixed all shell scripts calling functions before defining them, which is not
   portable.
                                                         (Manuel López-Ibáñez)

messages.body_plain:
Hello Rahul,

The ouput of your target runner (or the executable) you are using to run your algorithm must be only one number (or two in case you are providing execution time).

This error tells you that the output of the execution was:

Warning: integer...
0.2567...

Thus, your algorithm is printing this warning. This warning should not be in the result provided to irace.
You need modify your program / target runner so the warning is not part of the output provided to irace.

I hope this can help,

Bests,
Leslie.

messages.subject_clean: [irace-package] Re: Set-up for IRACE package using a '.exe' file

On Sunday, 22 July 2018 07:00:53 UTC-4, Rahul Roy wrote:
> Thank you Leslie!
>
> I'm surprised that this happened because I didn't make any changes and all the irace runs were executed successfully. But all of a sudden, twice this message has come and irace stopped therein. Should I include them in the forbidden configurations file? Can you kindly help me with the way the forbidden configurations should be written in the file as I couldn't get much help from the user guide? The parameters are specified in the snapshot attached in the previous mail.

Well, if you know that this warning means that the algorithm is not working properly then you should include this
configuration in the forbidden configurations file so irace will not try to test it. Before creating the file I would advice
you to try to understand which is the parameter value or the combination of parameter values that are causing this problem.
Once you know this you can create the file, lets assume that the problem is caused by the combination of the following parameters:

--METH1 ELLIPSOIDAL --PARA1 14.4541

so then the line in the forbidden configuration file should be:

(METH1 == "ELLIPSOIDAL") & (PARA1 == 14.4541)

Note that you should not use the flag of the parameter but the name, so this example assumes that the definition of the parameters is like this:

METH1   "--METH1 "  c  ("ELLIPSOIDAL", "OTHER")
PARA1   "--PARA1 "  r (0,20)

An alternative choice to the use of forbidden configurations would be to modify your target runner / executable to return Inf
(again, the warning should NOT be printed). This will make irace to reject the configuration that generated this Inf result.
This option is adviced when you dont know when the problem with your target algorithm happens. Check section 10.8 of the user guide for more details.

I hope this was useful.
Bests,
Leslie.
